source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A fairly ordinary, expected finding in this particular client that would not typically call for any urgent nursing action","B":"A fairly simple tension headache that would not typically be considered a time-sensitive clinical concern requiring intervention","C":"Autonomic dysreflexia, a potentially life-threatening emergency requiring immediate identification and removal of the triggering stimulus","D":"An improvement in the client's overall autonomic nervous system function reflected by this new symptom pattern appearing"}}
source_row.rationale: A severe pounding headache, profuse sweating/flushing above the level of injury, and significantly elevated blood pressure (typically 20-40 mmHg above the client's baseline) in a client with spinal cord injury at or above T6 are classic signs of autonomic dysreflexia, a potentially life-threatening emergency requiring immediate identification and removal of the triggering stimulus (most commonly bladder distention), along with positioning the client upright and loosening constrictive clothing.
source_row.source_detail: Classic Signs and Emergency Response to Autonomic Dysreflexia
